As the new school year begins, more Americans now support banning students from using phones entirely during class.

The new school year has started, and support for banning iPhones in the classroom is on the rise.

Yes, it's still July, but summer has somehow already ended. My own kids will head back to school today and tomorrow — making it the second summer in a row that the school year no longer begins in August.

Apple is welcoming the new school year with its annual Back to School promotion, offering eligible students and educators up to a $150 gift card when they purchase select Mac and iPad models. The promotion runs through August 27. Consumers in several states can also take advantage of limited-time sales tax holidays.

Although back-to-school discounts are popular, smartphone use during class is increasingly unpopular.

Top comment from GreenPizza

I've never seen any data suggesting that students using phones reduces the risk of school shootings. The everyday reality is that there are fewer distractions in class, allowing schools to actually fulfill their original educational mission.

A new Pew Research Center survey found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones during class. That number is up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Only 18% now oppose an in-class ban.

Support for stricter "all-day bans" has grown faster. For the first time, more Americans support than oppose banning phones for the entire school day.

The report also noted that younger Americans remain less enthusiastic about in-class bans and all-day bans, even though support has risen across all age groups since 2024. Click here to read the full report.

What do you think? Should schools limit iPhone use to class time only, implement an all-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Let us know in the comments.
